items.title: Sebi introduces fast-track process for securities transmission
items.description: Sebi has revised the securities transmission framework for investors.  A fast-track mechanism is introduced for small-value claims.  Documentation requirements are simplified, and probate of a will is removed.  Claims up to ₹10 lakh in physical and ₹30 lakh in demat form are covered.  This aims for a more efficient and investor-friendly process.

items.title: Private Bank ETFs back in focus as valuations turn attractive
items.description: Private bank stocks present a thematic investment opportunity with reasonable valuations.  These banks are showing improved margins and strong credit growth potential.  Analysts believe margin pressures are now behind the banking sector.  Credit growth is expected to accelerate significantly over the next two years.  Investors can consider accumulating private banks with a medium-term outlook.

items.title: North India leads India's expanding stock market investor base
items.description: North India now leads the nation in registered investors, surpassing the West. This significant shift accelerated after the pandemic with increased internet access. The North region saw its investor base expand six times since FY19. Maharashtra remains the largest state, though its share has declined. Uttar Pradesh has now overtaken Gujarat as the second-largest investor state.

items.title: Sebi plans a wider investment play for portfolio managers
items.description: The regulator said the review has been done due the rapid expansion of the PMS industry, where AUM (assets under management) has multiplied to ₹42.61 lakh crore as of May 2026 from ₹18.07 lakh crore in April 2019. "Considering the increasing sophistication of investors, growing demand for more personalised solutions and diverse investment portfolio, a need was felt to review the PM (portfolio manager) Regulations," Sebi said in a discussion paper on Thursday.

items.title: Regulator warns insurers against deep discounts on fire risk cover
items.description: The insurance regulator has flagged aggressive underpricing in fire insurance, with discounts of up to 99% on large industrial risks, warning it could hurt insurers’ financial health and underwriting discipline. Fire insurance premiums fell sharply in Q1 FY27 to ₹8,087 crore from ₹11,206 crore a year ago, after strong growth in FY26.

items.title: Fintechs tell NPCI its 'default app' plan could kill competition
items.description: Seven Indian fintech firms have written to NPCI regarding its UPI Meta protocol. They argue the proposed framework risks locking customers into a single default payment app. This change could adversely impact competition and innovation within the digital payments ecosystem. The companies request broader consultation before NPCI proceeds with the framework. They believe the current UPI checkout flow does not require such a significant alteration.

items.title: Godrej Capital aims to grow gold loan book to Rs 5000 crores by 2031
items.description: Godrej Capital aims to build a Rs 5,000 crore gold loan book.  This expansion follows their acquisition of Kanakadurga Finance's gold loan portfolio.  The company plans to increase its specialized gold loan branches to 350.  This strategy involves deepening presence in existing regions and launching new operations.  Godrej Capital targets a Rs 1 lakh crore overall AUM by 2031.

items.title: Three US law firms probe HDFC Bank over alleged Maharashtra deposit payments
items.description: HDFC Bank is facing fresh scrutiny in the US after three law firms launched investigations into whether the lender violated federal securities laws over allegations that it disguised ₹45 crore in payments to the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) as marketing expenses.

items.title: Ujjivan Small Finance Bank grows share of secured loan to over 50%
items.description: Ujjivan Small Finance Bank has achieved a significant milestone by increasing its secured loan portfolio. This strategic shift now represents over fifty percent of the bank's total loan book. The bank's gross loan book expanded by twenty-nine percent year-on-year. Ujjivan reported a three-fold jump in its first quarter net profit. Provisions were forty-three percent lower, aiding the profit growth.

items.title: IndiGo shares fall 2% after Rs 238 crore Q1 loss. So why are Citi and Nuvama raising target prices?
items.description: InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo) reported a Q1FY27 net loss of Rs 238 crore as soaring fuel costs pushed expenses ahead of revenue growth. Despite the earnings miss, brokerages including Citi and Nuvama retained their 'Buy' ratings and raised target prices, citing strong yields, pricing power, disciplined capacity expansion and long-term growth prospects driven by international expansion.

items.title: Why is market falling today? Sensex slumps over 700 points: 7 key factors behind Rs 3 lakh crore rout
items.description: Indian stock markets experienced sharp losses for a fifth straight session on Friday.  Sensex and Nifty indices saw significant drops, reflecting investor concerns.  Oil prices exceeding $100 per barrel and FII selling fueled the downturn.  Broader markets and specific sectors also registered substantial declines.  This selloff erased over Rs 3 lakh crore from market capitalization.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: Adani Power, JSW Energy among 5 stocks that could give 10-20% return
items.description: Domestic brokerages Emkay, Nuvama and JM Financial have maintained their bullish stance on select stocks across the asset management, banking, healthcare and power sectors.We have collated a list of recommendations from top brokerage firms from ETNow and other sources:

items.title: Meesho shares crack 5% as weak Q2 outlook spooks Street; Citi, Morgan Stanley react
items.description: Meesho shares fell after the company warned of slower NMV growth in the September quarter due to the rescheduling of its flagship festive sale and higher customer acquisition spending. While the outlook weighed on sentiment, the e-commerce firm narrowed its quarterly loss to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore a year earlier.

items.title: Infosys shares fall 3% as JPMorgan downgrades stock, Jefferies cuts target after Q1 results
items.description: Infosys shares fell after global brokerages turned cautious following the company's Q1 FY27 results and a cut to the upper end of its revenue growth guidance. JPMorgan downgraded the stock, while Jefferies lowered its target price, citing weaker demand visibility despite strong deal wins and rising AI-led revenue.

items.title: Motilal Oswal shares in focus after Q1 net profit rises 10%, AUM increases by 31%
items.description: Motilal Oswal Financial Services reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1,273 crore for Q1 FY27. Revenue from operations jumped over 25% year-on-year to Rs 3,426 crore during the quarter. The company achieved its highest ever operating profit after tax of Rs 1,513 crore. Its asset management business profit surged 73% to Rs 245 crore. The wealth management segment saw a 42% rise in Annual Recurring Revenue.

items.title: Manipal Health Enterprises sets price band for Rs 9,275 crore IPO, opens July 29
items.description: Manipal Health Enterprises will launch its Rs 9,275 crore IPO on July 29 with a price band of Rs 560-590 per share. The issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 8,000 crore and an OFS worth Rs 1,275.2 crore, with proceeds primarily earmarked for debt repayment and acquiring a minority stake in Sahyadri Hospitals.

items.title: Sebi proposes shifting ODR oversight to MIIs for quicker grievance redressal
items.description: Sebi proposes shifting online dispute resolution administration to market infrastructure institutions. This move aims to significantly speed up investor grievance redressal processes. Market infrastructure institutions will now handle conciliator and arbitrator appointments and oversight. Investors will have a voice in arbitrator selection, while conciliators are appointed directly. This framework change is estimated to shorten the overall resolution process by twenty-one days.

items.title: Dividend alert! Last day to buy Wipro, DLF, Persistent Systems among 12 stocks for dividend rewards. Do you own any?
items.description: IT major Wipro earlier this month announced an interim dividend of Rs 2 per equity share along with its Q1 results, with the record date being fixed on July 27. The company said its board of directors considered and approved a dividend of Rs 2 per equity share (face value Rs 2 each) during its meeting, which will be paid on or before August 14 this year.

items.title: Banking liquidity hits lowest since June 29; RBI data reveals Rs 2,884 crore deficit
items.description: Mumbai banking system liquidity has fallen to its lowest point since late June.  This deficit is attributed to increased credit growth and central bank foreign exchange market actions.  System liquidity experienced a deficit of ₹2,884 crore on Wednesday.  The Reserve Bank of India's intervention is expected to worsen this liquidity gap.  Economists anticipate further deficits in the coming days due to these factors.

items.title: NSE cash market turnover hits 23-month high in June
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced robust trading in June, reaching a 23-month high in cash market turnover. Proprietary traders' share of cash market turnover decreased, indicating broader investor participation. Foreign investors significantly increased their presence in equity futures, reaching a record high. Domestic institutional investors also boosted their share in equity futures during this period. Individual investors raised their participation in equity options, showing growing retail trader involvement.

items.title: Financials dominate Nifty50 in June, IT sector weight hits 23-year low
items.description: Financials increased their Nifty 50 weight to a four-month high in June. This rise followed sector outperformance and renewed foreign investor inflows. Information Technology continued its decline, losing significant weight in the index. The IT sector's weight is near a 23-year low due to global spending concerns. Weak global technology spending and AI disruption also impacted the IT sector.

items.title: Smaller stocks gain ground as largecaps lose market share
items.description: Large-cap stocks have seen their market share decline over six years. Mid, small, and micro-cap stocks have gained significant ground during this period. The Nifty's share of total market capitalization fell to a multi-year low. Meanwhile, the Nifty Smallcap 250 reached a multi-year high. This trend highlights the increasing weight of smaller companies in the market.

items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Domestic equities extended losses for a fourth consecutive session, with the Nifty declining. Investor sentiment remained fragile amid a sharp surge in Brent crude oil prices. Foreign portfolio investors net sold shares worth Rs 2,999 crore on Wednesday. The rupee traded in a narrow range, appreciating marginally by around 0.05%. Analysts suggest Indian equities are likely to remain under pressure in the near term.

items.title: Stocks in news: Infosys, Cipla, Meesho, Suzlon Energy, IndiGo, NTPC
items.description: Markets extended their losing streak for a fourth consecutive session. Infosys reported a 12% year-on-year profit growth in its first quarter. Cipla's net profit fell 39% due to weakness in its North America business. IndiGo reported a loss of Rs 238 crore in its first quarter. Several other companies will announce their first quarter results today.

items.title: AI Powerplay! Proxy power stocks give up to 100% returns in India's hottest trade this year
items.description: India's power and electrical equipment stocks have emerged as key AI proxy plays, with names like Hitachi Energy, Kirloskar Oil Engines and GE Vernova T&D delivering stellar returns. Analysts believe rising data centre investments will fuel long-term demand, but caution that valuations and stock selection will be critical from here.

items.title: Lohia Corp IPO subscribed 43% on Day 2 so far. Here’s what latest GMP trends indicate
items.description: Lohia Corp IPO  GMP Day 2: Lohia Corp's initial public offering is experiencing decent investor interest on its second day. The Rs 1,101 crore maiden issue has been subscribed 43% so far. Retail investors are leading the subscription numbers, booking 80% of their reserved portion. Unlisted shares are trading with a muted grey market premium of 3-8.5%. The company manufactures machinery for technical textile production and reported strong financial growth.

items.title: Ashish Kacholia's Q1 portfolio: 13 stocks the ace investor bought, sold or likely exited. Full list
items.description: Ace investor Ashish Kacholia reshuffled his portfolio in the first quarter of FY27 amid a rapidly changing geopolitical landscape. Shareholding data from Trendlyne shows the market veteran added new stocks, increased his holdings in some companies, trimmed stakes in others, and likely exited four stocks during Q1FY27. Here's the full list of stocks bought and sold by the 'Big Whale'.

items.title: Ashish Kacholia exits defence stock that rallied 108% in Q1. Do you own it?
items.description: Veteran investor Ashish Kacholia appears to have exited Walchandnagar Industries in Q1 FY27, as his name is absent from the heavy engineering firm's June-quarter shareholding data—implying his holding has slipped below the 1% disclosure threshold.

items.title: Q1 Results today: SBI Life, Tata Consumer, Hindustan Zinc among 86 companies to announce earnings
items.description: A total of 86 companies are slated to announce their Q1 FY27 earnings today, with key names including Tata Consumer Products, SBI Life Insurance, Hindustan Zinc, Shriram Finance, ACC, Bank of Baroda, Bank of India, SAIL, SBI Cards, Laurus Labs and Lodha Developers.

items.title: Mukesh Ambani’s long game: How Reliance could turn a 3-year spending spree into Rs 90,000 crore of free cash flow
items.description: Reliance Industries could generate nearly Rs 90,000 crore in cumulative free cash flow over FY26-FY28 as its heavy investment cycle eases, brokerages say. Stronger earnings from energy and Jio, coupled with moderating capex, may reduce leverage and mark the beginning of a sustained cash flow and earnings upcycle.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold? Citi maintains buy on Meesho; Elara Capital recommends buy on Vishal Mega Mart
items.description: Brokerages issued fresh post-earnings calls on three stocks. Citi raised its Meesho target to Rs 220 (17% upside) based on strong pricing power. Elara Capital maintained a Buy rating on Vishal Mega Mart, setting a target of Rs 159 (44% upside) after an in-line quarter. Morgan Stanley maintained an Underweight rating on Cyient (Rs 820), preferring to see a sustained growth recovery despite a better-than-feared performance.

items.title: Caliber Mining and Logistics shares list at 19% premium over IPO price on BSE
items.description: Caliber Mining & Logistics shares debuted nearly 19% above their IPO price on Friday, beating grey market expectations. The Rs 450 crore issue was subscribed 156.63 times, driven by strong demand across investor categories. The company plans to use the IPO proceeds to reduce debt, fund expansion, and strengthen operations.

items.title: Forget selling! FIIs doubled down on this AI multibagger stock that's up 200% YTD
items.description: HFCL has emerged as a favourite among foreign investors, with FIIs more than doubling their stake to 15.7% in Q1 despite the stock surging 200% in 2026. Strong AI-driven data centre demand, record order book, robust earnings, capacity expansion and growing defence ambitions have prompted brokerages to turn bullish, with Deven Choksey seeing another 75% upside.

items.title: Why Swiggy shares fell over 5% today: Foreign ownership cap sparks $460 million passive outflow fears
items.description: Swiggy shares fell after the company proposed cutting its foreign ownership limit to 49.5% from 100%, raising concerns over its eligibility for major global indices. The move could lead to Swiggy's exclusion from the MSCI Standard and FTSE indices, triggering an estimated $460 million in passive outflows, according to reports.

items.title: HDFC Bank, 3 other bank stocks wipe out Rs 1.5 lakh crore of investors' wealth after Q1. Time to buy the dip?
items.description: Shares of HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Yes Bank have erased over Rs 1.5 lakh crore in market value this week following their June-quarter earnings. While investors reacted negatively to the results amid broader market weakness, brokerages say the sharp correction has made valuations more attractive, with Axis Bank emerging as a preferred pick.

items.title: Chris Wood warns of massive capital destruction in US as China challenges AI boom
items.description: Jefferies strategist Chris Wood warns that the AI infrastructure boom could trigger massive capital destruction as cheaper Chinese open-source models challenge US dominance. With hyperscalers set to spend nearly $1.6 trillion over two years, investors are increasingly questioning whether returns will justify the unprecedented capex and rising debt.

items.title: SBI Funds Management shares fall below IPO price, but brokerages remain bullish. Time to buy?
items.description: SBI Funds Management shares slipped below their IPO price after listing, but brokerages remain bullish on the stock, citing strong parentage, a vast distribution network, sticky SIP flows, robust profitability and long-term mutual fund growth opportunities.

items.title: Caliber Mining shares drop 8% after listing with 19% premium over IPO price. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: Caliber Mining and Logistics shares fell over 8% after debuting at a 19% premium to their IPO price. Despite the post-listing correction, analysts advise IPO allottees to hold for the medium to long term, while fresh investors should wait for a dip or consolidation before considering fresh exposure.

items.title: HDFC Bank shares fall as 3 US law firms launch probe over alleged federal law violations
items.description: Three United States law firms are investigating HDFC Bank for alleged securities law violations. These firms are examining if the bank disguised payments to MSRDC as marketing expenses. HDFC Bank shares have declined significantly following these announcements and after its Q1 earnings report. The bank has strongly denied any allegations of wrongdoing or culpability. Investigations are ongoing, with firms seeking shareholders who suffered losses to come forward.

items.title: India regulator bars former Axis MF dealer for seven years in front-running case
items.description: India's financial watchdog has penalized former Axis Mutual Fund chief dealer Viresh Joshi with a hefty thirty million rupee fine for leaking sensitive trading data. Joshi allegedly collaborated with others to execute a coordinated front-running scheme from 2021 to 2022, utilizing mule accounts and WhatsApp to make illicit profits from fund transactions. As a consequence, the regulator has barred him from participating in securities markets for the next seven years.

items.title: Market wrap: HCLTech, Bajaj Finance, Eternal among top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Friday
items.description: Indian equities fell for a fifth straight session as Brent crude stayed above $100, FII selling and global concerns weighed on sentiment. Analysts warned of persistent volatility, rising inflation risks and a deeper correction if Nifty slips below the 23,600 support.
